why: Inserting the fallback that prefers punctuation/clause-boundary cuts as a last resort made the model favor clause/punctuation boundaries more often, producing a small net improvement concentrated on short pieces (largest gains in the ≤3 and ≤5 bins) but also shifting many kept cuts so they now split numerals/units or separate finite verbs from their immediately following complements, which explains the sizable set of worse (but more localized) degradations.
lesson: A later revision should keep the punctuation/clause-boundary preference that helped short pieces while ensuring it does not override protections that keep numerals attached to their units or finite verbs attached to their core complements.
